en: Dependent on a state that is not conducive to fettering (*nasaññojaniya*), a state that is not conducive to fettering arises by way of the root condition (*hetupaccaya*).
Dependent on a state that is not conducive to fettering, a state that is not non-conducive to fettering arises by way of the root condition.
Dependent on a state that is not conducive to fettering, states that are both not conducive to fettering and not non-conducive to fettering arise by way of the root condition.
Dependent on a state that is not a fetter-inducing factor (*asaññojaniya*), a state that is not a fetter-inducing factor arises by way of the root condition (*hetupaccaya*).
Dependent on a state that is both a fetter-inducing and not a fetter-inducing factor, a state that is not a fetter-inducing factor arises by way of the root condition. (Abbreviated.
There are five [types of relations] under the root condition, two under the object condition ... pe ... five under the non-disappearance condition. (Full detail for all cases.)
